title: on open PDFs from studio, could those tabs get their own icon i.e. different from the main home icon that we have for studio tabs? it should be a minimal simple icon that denotes PDF.
note: The PDF tab icon is now the pink 'PDF' pill from the Files tab: soft pink with the letters in the same rose. It wasn't showing before because the icon was only an SVG, and some browsers (Safari among them) skip an SVG icon and fall back to their own PDF glyph. It now ships as PNGs too (16, 32 and 48 px, plus a large one for Safari), which every browser takes, and the URL is versioned so a cached older icon isn't reused. Caveat: I couldn't watch a real tab strip from here - if a PDF tab still shows the browser's own icon after a reload, tell me which browser it is (Safari, Chrome, Edge) and I'll chase it there.

title: for the animated pop up from alt s, the play button doesnt really make sense to display here. can we make this pop up look sleeker
note: The ⌥S pop-up is now a slim pill: a small rust dot that pings when a session starts and then gently pulses, 'Session started' (or 'Already studying' if one was running), a hairline, and the clock. The big rust circle with the play button is gone - there was nothing to press, the session was already going. Same place, same rise-and-sink animation, same timing.

title: if we move a project meeting that has prep items, ensure that we move their due dates to the new meeting i.e. ensure the tasks are tied to that meeting so we dont have to manually update them
note: Moving a meeting now makes every open prep task due at the meeting's new time - including ones that had been set for an earlier day, so nothing is left offset. Undated prep gets the meeting time too. Done, cancelled and backlogged prep stays where it was, and prep on Google Calendar has its event moved. It only happens when the date or time changes: renaming a meeting or changing its location leaves the prep dates alone. Action items keep their own dates.

title: Instead of the file icon for markdown notes in the files tab of a task/nexus, can we display an md pill similar in style to the PDF bill (but of course different colour)
note: Markdown notes now carry a green 'MD' pill in the Files tab and the Nexus, in the same style as the PDF, DOCX and PPTX pills, instead of the little page icon. It's in both views: at the start of the row in Tree, and in the card's footer in Gallery, where file cards already showed theirs. Green, because pink, blue and amber are already PDF, Word and PowerPoint. An uploaded .md file gets the same pill.

title: On the home page, can we ensure that the key states do not get pushed onto two lines? Adjust their font size as required or change the display for smaller viewports? Just want them to read across one line
note: The home page's key stats (Today, This week, Streak, Avg focus) now always read on one line each - labels, numbers and the line underneath. Two changes: when there isn't room for them beside Overall progress, they drop below it at full width instead of squeezing into narrow columns (which is what wrapped 'This week', 'Avg focus' and '0 sessions logged'), and they sit two-by-two below about 768px wide. The numbers also scale down a little with their column, so a long one like '38h 05m' shrinks rather than breaking. Checked from phone width up to 1440px with long values filled in.

title: The keyboards shortcut does not seem to be working for changing between live and markdown in the task md file.
note: ⌥M now switches between Live and Markdown - in task and todo notes, Nexus notes, lectures, and the smaller markdown fields. The old ⌘⇧M / Ctrl-Shift-M wasn't broken in Studio: Chrome and Edge keep that combination for their profile menu, so the page never saw the keypress. ⌘⇧M still works where the browser lets it through, and the Live / Markdown buttons' tooltips now say ⌥M.

title: Can we make sure the markdown textarea takes up the full height (or just about) of the screen instead of getting randomly cut off? This will be global across all note taking instances in the site
note: The Markdown view's text box now grows with the note instead of stopping at a fixed 60% of the screen and scrolling inside itself - that inner scroll was the 'random' cut-off. The page scrolls instead, so the whole note is always there to read and select. A short note still gets a box that reaches the bottom of the screen, so there's room to write. This is the one editor behind lecture notes, Nexus notes and task and todo notes, so it applies to all of them; the smaller markdown fields (meeting agendas, paper and reading notes) grow the same way but start at their own small size rather than filling the screen.

title: Allow the creation of a focus mode. This is where I am studying and I want to go into ultra focus mode. Studio becomes ultra minimal and only gives me access to the task I have picked i.e. only the project page, or only a course page with its lecture. Upon selection of the task, I select an amount o
note:
Focus mode is in, behind one new button on the timer bar - the three dots where the full-screen button was. Click it and three options fan out above the bar: Ultra focus, Full screen and Pause.

Ultra focus: pick what to lock to (the Project or any course) and for how long (25m, 50m, 1h30 or 2h), then Start ultra focus. Studio jumps to that page and strips down to it: the nav, search (⌘K), quick-add, the due-soon banner, the last-lecture shortcut and the ⌥Q queue all disappear, and a slim bar at the top shows what you're locked to and the time left. A course lock allows its page and its own lectures and tasks; the Project lock allows everything under Project. Anything else - home, the calendar, another course, Livio - sends you straight back, whether you click a link, type the address or reload; that's checked on the server, so there's no way round it in the browser. It lifts on its own when the time runs out, or when you end the session with the stop button. The discard button is hidden while it's on, so ending means logging the session.

Pause: stops the clock without ending the session. The timer shows PAUSED and the dot becomes a play button to resume (or use Resume in the menu, or ⌥S). Paused time is never counted - it comes off the session when you log it.

Full screen is the same studying view as before, just moved into the menu.

Caveat: pausing doesn't stop the ultra-focus countdown - the lock is wall-clock time.

title: A big big feature. I'd like to have a new tab for the Claude knowledge base for the project.
note:
Built: Project → Claude, a knowledge base kept in its own private repo (OllieL1/kb), so any Claude session on any machine can read it, and Claude can edit and push it too. Studio shows those changes the next time the tab opens.

Browsing: the Nexus browser (gallery or tree), with the repo's real folders in place of tags. The folder chips are the top-level folders, each including its subfolders, and your pick is remembered: choose msci-project once and the tab opens on it. Cards show the word count and file name ("12 words · INDEX.md").

Editing: what you type is a draft, saved as you go exactly like a note, so it survives leaving the page and follows the stick. Nothing reaches GitHub until you commit. A live, GitHub-style diff above the editor shows what's uncommitted, and Discard goes back to GitHub's version. Changed docs show a dot and +added −removed in the tree and gallery, folders get a dot too, and an "Uncommitted" bar above the browser lists them, each opening to its diff.

Committing: ⌘S opens one dialog listing every uncommitted doc with a tick, plus a message box. From inside a doc only that doc is ticked; on the tab, all of them are. Everything ticked goes in one commit. New docs are drafts too, so a doc and its first content land in the same commit. Renames and deletes commit straight away. If Claude changed a doc on GitHub after you started editing it, the doc is marked "behind GitHub", and nothing is committed until you choose Use GitHub's or Keep mine for it.

Studio writes only the files you commit. Your INDEX.md files are yours.

Getting it into sessions: ~/kb is cloned on WSL; add the SessionStart hook from the README ("The Claude knowledge base") to pull it and print INDEX.md.

Caveat: if you're editing the same doc in two windows at once, the one that saved last wins its draft, just as with notes.

title: Can we rename the tab to KB instead of Claude?
note: Renamed: the Project tab is now KB, and a doc's back link says ← KB. The addresses moved with it (/project?tab=kb, /project/kb?path=…); the old ?tab=claude and /project/claude links still work and land in the same place, so bookmarks and open tabs are fine. The code follows suit - KbTab and KbBrowser instead of ClaudeTab and ClaudeKb. Your remembered view and folder filter carry over.

title: Ensure we add the ability for PDF export for each note just like each of the other notes uses. It can just use our existing PDF renderer.
note: Each KB doc has a PDF button in its toolbar, next to GitHub ↗. It opens the PDF in its own tab, through the same renderer as Nexus notes: the title once (taken from the doc's # heading), the word count and last update, the repo and the doc's path along the top of each page. It's the doc as it is in Studio - uncommitted changes included, down to what you typed a second ago (that's saved first). Per doc only; there's no bundle export.

title: Add autocomplete when typing out a new note for the tag names i.e. if I start typing ms then I should be able to press tab to autocomplete msci-project/
note: The new-doc box completes folder names as you type. Start a name with ms and the rest - ci-project/ - shows in grey after the caret; Tab (or → at the end) takes it. It goes one folder at a time like a shell: after msci-project/, typing n completes msci-project/notes/ and so on. When two folders share the start (misc and msci-project after m), Tab fills in as far as they agree, and if they split straight away it does nothing and Tab moves on as normal. Case doesn't matter - MS completes too. The Rename box on a doc completes the same way, so moving a doc into a folder is quick. The old dropdown of folders is gone - the completion replaces it.

title: Improve the dropdown for read/reading/to read to be site native and better align with the design of the rest of the site
note: The reading-status pill on each paper now opens Studio's own small menu instead of the browser's grey native list: To read / Reading / Read, each with its colour dot and a tick on the current one. The pill changes straight away, while the save happens in the background. It works from the keyboard too: ↓ opens it, ↑↓ move, Enter picks and Esc backs out. The menu floats over the page, so it isn't cut off on the last paper in the list, and scrolling closes it.

title: The settings has got a bit hectic.
note: Settings now has a sidebar on the left, laid out like a file tree, and the section you pick opens on the right. It opens on Appearance. Connectors is a folder holding GitHub, Google Calendar, Spotify and Pushcut. Backup sits under Data, and Enhancements and Semester 2 are at the bottom. Each section is its own page (e.g. /settings/github), so it can be linked to and survives a reload, and it only loads its own data - so the Google calendar list is no longer fetched every time you open Settings for something else. Links elsewhere in Studio (Connect Google Calendar, the GitHub tab, Spotify on the stats page, search) now go straight to the right section, as do the Google and Spotify sign-in round trips. Old /settings#github-style links still find their way. On a phone the tree becomes a row of buttons above the section.

title: can we improve the title editing such that we remove the edit button but if i click on the title (when rendered) then i can edit it i.e.
note: The Edit button is gone: click the title and it turns into a text box in the same place and size. Enter (or clicking away) saves; Esc puts the old title back. Hovering the title shows a soft band so it reads as clickable, and it can be reached with Tab and opened with Enter too. This is the same note editor everywhere, so Nexus notes behave the same way.

title: the PDF export when rendering numbered lists is quite bugged.
note: Both came from the same bug: the number's box was 8pt wide, so "10." didn't fit and broke one character per line. Past 10 that stacked the digits down the margin. At the foot of a page the overflow started a new page by itself, and the item was then drawn back at the old bottom position on the new page - hence the blank page with one line at the very bottom. The number now sits right-aligned in a gutter wide enough for two digits (so 9. and 10. line up and the text doesn't shift), drawn as one run that can't wrap or break the page. A list crossing a page carries on at the top of the next one. Checked against the retro Plan note.

title: double nested lists do not render properly in the PDF.
note: Nesting depth was the leading spaces halved and capped at two levels, with "–" for everything below the top, so a third and fourth level sat exactly on the second. Depth now counts indent steps from the items above (the editor's two spaces, three under a number, four, or tabs all work), every level steps in, and coming back out lines up with the level it belongs to. The first four bullet levels have their own markers: • ◦ ▪ –, and deeper levels cycle round. Numbered items keep the numbers you wrote at any depth. Checked against the retro Plan note.

title: The text area should not be visible when the text is saved for the title of a note i.e. it should only appear or be visible when editing after a click.
note: The soft hover band behind a note's title is gone. With the pointer still resting on a title you'd just saved, it looked like a text box left open. Now the title is plain text until you click it, and the bordered box only appears while you're editing. The text cursor still shows it's clickable, and Tab + Enter still opens it. Same note editor in Studio, Nexus and Livio todo notes.

title: we do not render checkboxes in the rendered PDFs - they just render raw as - []. please can we fix this?
note: Task-list items in exported PDFs now get a real checkbox instead of the raw '- [ ]' text. An open item gets an outlined box, a done one ([x]) a filled box with a white tick. Each box sits in the bullet's place, so nested to-dos still step in level by level. Plain bullets and numbered items are unchanged. This covers every PDF that renders markdown: notes, lectures and reading notes.

title: massive massive bug. lets say i am writing a note, i ctrl k to another note and then i hit the back button in the browser.
note:
What was wrong: Back (and Forward) brings a page back as it was when you first opened it, not as you left it. The editor took that old copy as "what's saved", and its first blur or autosave wrote it straight over everything since. Nothing on the server checked. That's how Peer Reviews went back to its 11:27 heading-and-empty-quote at 11:48. The 11:42 version was recovered from the database's write-ahead log.

What changed, in two layers:
- Every save now says what it expects to replace, and the server only writes if that's still what's stored. If not, nothing is written, saving stops, and a "Not saved" banner offers Copy this version and Reload. It covers notes on tasks and in Nexus, and lecture notes. It also catches two tabs on the same note.
- When an editor opens, it reads what's stored now. If the page was a stale copy and you haven't typed yet, it shows the latest text instead. So Back now lands on what you last wrote.

Caveat: renaming a tag rewrites mentions inside note bodies, so a note open in another tab during a rename will show the banner. Reload it.

title: i have recently got a job with Sovrano under dataannotation.
note:
Sovrano is here: time tracking for paid work, in Livio, with the timer working in Studio too.

Timing: ⌥W starts a work session from any page in either app, even while you're typing. A teal bar appears bottom-left (study stays rust and centred) and counts up, with pause and stop. Press ⌥W again, or click stop, to log it. When nothing is running, the bar shrinks to a small "Work ⌥W" chip. The two timers never count the same minute: starting or resuming study pauses work, and resuming work pauses study. You resume the paused one yourself. Rapt Mode hides the work bar.

Logging asks for four things only: a name, a project (pick one, or "+ New project" to make one there and then), Sovrano or DataAnnotation, and the duration. The duration uses the same down-only bar as study. The most recent project is picked to start with, along with the platform you last used for it. When the project has a rate, the button shows what the session is worth.

The page (Livio → Sovrano) shows:
- Owed ($ and unpaid hours), this week, this month, all time (split by platform) and paid to date.
- A projects table: click a rate to set it in USD/h, click a name to filter to it, double-click a name to rename it.
- Every session, as a keyboard table like Reading. Edit name, project, platform and time (time only goes down). p marks a session paid or unpaid, ⌫ deletes it (u to undo).

Commands:
- :paid marks everything unpaid in the current view as paid, after a confirm that shows the hours and $. Filter to a project first to pay just that one. :unpaid reverses it.
- :rate 24.50 sets the rate for the filtered project.
- :project Acme 30 adds a project.
- :log 1h20 batch 4 logs work you didn't time (see below).
- :export (or the PDF button) opens the view as a PDF: totals, a per-project breakdown, then every session. :export json (or the JSON button) downloads the same data as a file.

Money: unpaid time uses each project's current rate. Marking a session paid freezes its amount, so changing a rate later only changes what's still owed. Time on a project with no rate shows "no rate", not $0, and isn't counted in the owed total until you set one. A paid session can't be moved to another project or have its time changed until you mark it unpaid.

Forgot to start the timer? :log 1h20 rubric batch opens the same dialog for past work: set the day and start time, and type the length (45, 1h20 or 1:20). It can't end in the future. :stop opens the log for the running session.

Caveat: it needs a database migration, which the next deploy applies.
